newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Malbak shareholders approve unbundling.
newsitem.headline: Malbak shareholders approve unbundling.

text.p: Shareholders in South Africa's diversified industrial holding company Malbak Ltd have approved the process to unbundle its assets, the company said on Monday.
Shareholders gave approval at a meeting last week for the company to sell its unlisted subsidiaries and investments and its investment in Haggie Ltd, a company statement said.
It warned shareholders to continue to exercise caution in their share dealings, pending consideration of formal offers for Malbak's listed companies.

The shareholders authorised Malbak directors to sell the company's assets on such terms and conditions as they deem fit, "provided that any sale to associated companies or persons or employees is considered to be fair and reasonable by the advisers to the unbundling, Rand Merchant Bank and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell".
Acting chief executive Peter Beningfield said negotiaitons on the unlisted companies were progressing well and an announcement could be expected in a few weeks.

He said South Africa's exchange control regulations inhibit the distribution of its 64 percent stake in London-listed MY Holdings Plc and the company's directors and advisers would examine their options.

In terms of the unbundling plan unveiled by Beningfield at the end of October, for every 100 Malbak shares held, shareholders would receive approximately 11.2 shares in Foodcorp Ltd, 61.2 shares in Kohler Ltd, 13.8 shares in South African Druggists Ltd, 14 in Ellerine Ltd and 36.2 in New Clicks Ltd.
Malbak shareholders will meet in March 1997 to approve the implementation of the unbundling, the statement added.
